feature: Small items 2, item 8 and small items 3, item 8: quick-add's failed search says so in the shared deck toast, with Try again, and every deck toast stands in one stack 10px above the quick-add dock (the receipt on the floor, the one alert above it)
note: Run against a deck the signed-in account owns (QAF_DECK). The search is a Server Action POSTed to the deck's own URL, so the failure is forced by mocking that URL with a 500 AFTER the page has loaded; the toasts render into the shell's deck toast stack, outside `main`, so each row waits on it with `waitToast`. The page is reused across rows, so each row unroutes its mock last. Its rows write nothing. The receipt with the failed search above it is not photographed: a receipt only arrives from a write (Bought adds a copy and takes the row off Shopping), and the runner has no cleanup that restores a row's writes between cells or after a failed one (`clearAbout` is its only restore), so the phone cell would spend the fixture row the desktop cell needs and every run would leave the account a copy richer. The pair (the receipt on the floor, the alert 10px above it, whichever mounted first, and a receipt leaving the failed search standing) is proved by deck-toast-stack.test.tsx; i-got-it.json photographs the receipt itself, from the stack, on its scratch branch. `refusal-failed` presses a row's ✕ under the same 500, which the server answers as a refused removal: nothing is written. The press is outside the bar, so it clears the field (and the failed search with it); the refusal is the one alert left, never a third toast.

shares.note: The deck slot's toast frame, the one the got-it receipt draws. The failed-search toast renders it as-is (placement "deck"), never a copy of its look.

rows.label: /decks/[id]: a quick-add search that failed. The toast stands 10px above the dock; the field keeps "sw" and focus, no list opens
/decks/[id]: the same failure, then a search that lands (typing on). The toast is gone and the list opens
/decks/[id]: a removal refused while the failed search was up. The refusal takes the one alert's place, 10px above the dock
